products.us_shipping_note: Two US profiles cover variant 87922: 9.59 first item / 2.69 additional, and 11.39 first item / 3.09 additional. The gate fails on the cheaper profile, so the conclusion holds either way.

economics_gate.severity: The product is underwater at the target price - it loses $5.07 per unit before a single marketplace fee. This is not a few points short of the gate.
economics_gate.merchandise_only_note: Even ignoring shipping entirely, merchandise margin is 13.7% against a 45% gate.
economics_gate.market_judgment: A ~$69-72 retail for a 1000-piece art puzzle is far outside the Etsy competitive band (comparable adult art puzzles commonly sit around $25-45). Repricing to clear the gate would price the product out of its market, so autonomous repricing does not rescue this.

root_cause.finding: The package's reference economics were built on the catalogue 'from' figures, which belong to the 110-piece variant, not the 1014-piece variant this batch targets.
root_cause.evidence: Package reference public_catalog_start_price_usd 8.39 and public_shipping_from_usd 5.99 are EXACTLY variant 87919 (110 pcs Horizontal): server-verified cost 8.39, US shipping 5.99. The 1014-piece variant 87922 is server-verified at cost 28.47 and US shipping 9.59.
root_cause.note: The package's own preflight_required list anticipated this exact trap: 'Do not treat the catalog from price as the 1014-piece cost.' The preflight caught it; the target retail was set before it was caught.

mechanical_corrections_applied: Package tag 'dark aesthetic puzzle' is 21 characters and would be silently rejected by Etsy's 20-character cap. Shortened to 'dark aesthetic'. Factual channel-constraint correction only; no creative change.
non_blocking_findings: Printify reports 11041042 bytes for the uploaded master vs 11041060 at source - an 18-byte delta, the same ancillary-marker stripping seen on MM-20260909-004. Dimensions verified 8700x5768 and render QC scored crop and scale 10/10, so this is not corruption.
Creating a product on blueprint 1149 auto-populates all 8 variants. Only 87922 is enabled, as instructed; the other 7 remain disabled and carry Printify's default price=cost.
The draft product was deliberately NOT deleted. It holds the verified cost, the correct 1:1 placement and a passing render QC, so a repriced or re-scoped relaunch can reuse it instead of rebuilding.
products.state_preserved: Draft product 6aa202384338f2e83c05ced6 exists in Printify shop 28809600, unpublished and not visible to any customer. No listing was created on any marketplace. Nothing is live.

decision_required_from_dandre.option_a: Reprice the 1014-piece to $69.20+ and publish. Clears the gate but prices the product well above the competitive band for a 1000-piece puzzle.
decision_required_from_dandre.option_b: Re-scope to the 520-piece horizontal (variant 87921) at ~$45.49, or the 252-piece (87920) at ~$34.82. Both clear 45%. NOTE: this requires a new package - the master is 8700x5768 and the 520/252 placeholders are 6300x5100 and 4395x3450, so ChatGPT Creative must confirm the downscale or supply a matched master. I did not change the variant myself; the package locks 87922.
decision_required_from_dandre.option_c: Keep the 1014-piece but accept a lower margin gate for a premium collectible positioning - e.g. $49.99 yields 23.9% gross before fees. This is an owner economics decision, not an execution one.
decision_required_from_dandre.option_d: Seek a cheaper print provider for blueprint 1149 and re-run the economics.
decision_required_from_dandre.recommendation: Option B at the 520-piece, or Option A only if you want the collectible positioning to carry the price. The blocker is a supplier cost fact, not a creative or execution fault - render QC passed at 92 and the artwork is untouched.

products.remaining_blocker: Verified 1014-piece landed cost $38.06 against a $32.99 target retail. Publishing would sell every unit at a $5.07 loss.

queue_note: Queue record deliberately left IN_PROGRESS, not COMPLETE and not FAILED. COMPLETE can never be reopened and nothing was published; FAILED is terminal and requires an external requeue, while this is fully recoverable by a pricing or variant decision. The claim is retained so execution can resume at the publish step once the economics are resolved.
